title: Quantile-driven crossplane negotiator for multi-GPU prefetch and NCCL overlap
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Multi-GPU prefill/decode workloads suffer high tail latency when tensor- and pipeline-parallel stages contend for NCCL and kernel execution windows. Existing heuristics (static windows, fixed rendezvous points) either over-reserve NCCL bandwidth (hurting throughput) or underlap (increasing tail latency).
goal: Design and implement a crossplane negotiation layer that dynamically allocates short NCCL overlap windows and prefetch handoffs based on observed per-token latency quantiles and workload phase, while exposing kernel-selection hints for attention microkernels to reduce stall variance.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end integrated scheduler in runtime repo behind feature flag
Measured 95th-percentile token-latency reduction >= 8% on long-sequence chat benchmark compared to baseline (no negotiation)
No >5% regression in overall token throughput at p50 under the same benchmark
Graceful fallback to current rendezvous logic when NCCL resources unavailable or when feature-flag disabled
Unit/integration tests for crossplane negotiation logic + regression test added to CI
design_notes: High-level approach: (1) Maintain lightweight running quantiles for token latencies per stage (p50,p90,p95). (2) When prefill/early-decode phases are detected, negotiate micro-overlap windows sized to the upper quantile of expected communication time + safety margin (configurable). (3) Emit kernel-selection hints to attention microkernels (epilogue vs fused attention variants) to reduce compute tail in contested windows. (4) Backpressure: if NCCL congestion detected, reduce overlap aggressiveness and prioritize progress on pipeline leader stages.
tradeoffs: Aggressive overlap reduces tail latency but increases NCCL memory pressure and can harm throughput for highly concurrent workloads. Quantile estimation adds small CPU overhead and state; we bound it to per-worker lightweight sketches to limit overhead. Kernel hinting requires additional kernel-selection logic (adds complexity) but keeps compute tails smaller than naive overlap.
implementation_plan: 1) Spike: implement quantile estimator + synthetic microbench (2w). 2) Prototype negotiator + kernel hint interface behind feature flag (3w). 3) Integrate with NCCL controller and pipeline coordinator; add telemetry hooks (2w). 4) Run canary on dedicated cluster, gather metrics, iterate (2w).
benchmarks: Spike results (internal): on synthetic long-context prefill workload (seq=4096, batch=4, model=redwood-13b-quant), early prototype reduced p95 token latency by 12% but increased NCCL memory high-water by ~7% and showed a 3% throughput dip at p50. Next tuning aims to recover throughput with adaptive window shrinkback.
